questions.q: What must be true about a masking policy's RETURNS type and the column it's attached to?
options: They must match exactly — a policy returning STRING can't be attached to a DATE column
They can be any compatible type, Snowflake converts automatically
RETURNS type only matters for numeric columns
There is no relationship between the two
questions.explain: A masking policy's RETURNS type must match the signature (val) type, and both must match the target column's data type — Snowflake needs the masked output to remain a legal value for that column.

questions.q: In the real tasty_pii_string_mask policy, what happens when CURRENT_ROLE() is ACCOUNTADMIN or SYSADMIN?
options: The value is always masked regardless of role
The CASE expression returns val unchanged — the real value
The query fails with a permissions error
The column is dropped from the result
questions.explain: The first WHEN branch checks for ACCOUNTADMIN or SYSADMIN and returns val as-is — those roles see the real value, and the CASE exits before reaching the tag-based branches.

questions.q: What does SYSTEM$GET_TAG_ON_CURRENT_COLUMN('TAGS.TASTY_PII') let the policy's CASE expression do?
options: Count how many rows match the current filter
Read the TASTY_PII tag value attached to the specific column being queried, so the policy can branch on it
Automatically generate a new masking policy
Check whether the warehouse is currently suspended
questions.explain: SYSTEM$GET_TAG_ON_CURRENT_COLUMN reads the tag value on the column currently being evaluated, letting one policy apply different masking logic depending on what each column is tagged as — phone number vs email, for example.

questions.q: Which command attaches a masking policy directly to a column without using a tag?
options: SHOW MASKING POLICIES
DESCRIBE MASKING POLICY
ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN ... SET MASKING POLICY
CREATE TAG
questions.explain: ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN ... SET MASKING POLICY attaches a policy straight to a column. UNSET MASKING POLICY removes it again. Neither requires a tag.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what's true about whether a policy was attached directly vs. via a tag, from the perspective of the querying role?
options: The querying role sees a warning indicating which method was used
It's completely invisible — only the resulting masking behavior is visible, not the assignment mechanism
Tag-based policies run twice as slow
Direct assignment only works for DATE columns
questions.explain: Whether a masking policy reached a column directly or through a tag is invisible at query time — the querying role only ever sees the masked (or unmasked) result, never how the policy got attached.
